summary: Sculk sensors only detect the last turtle egg being broken when being stepped on
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft 1.18.2 and enter a world.
2. Place four turtle eggs on the same block.
3. Place a sculk sensor near the turtle eggs.
4. Stand on top of the turtle eggs.
5. Wait until the turtle eggs break.
6. Observe whether the sculk sensor activates as the turtle eggs break, including when the last turtle egg is broken.
Environment: Minecraft Java Edition Versions: 20w51a, 21w03a, 21w05a, 21w05b, 21w06a, 21w07a, 21w08b, 21w10a, 21w14a, 21w15a, 21w17a, 21w19a, 21w20a, 1.17 Pre-release 1, 1.17 Release Candidate 1, 1.17 Release Candidate 2, 1.17, 1.17.1 Pre-release 1, 1.17.1, 1.18, 1.18.1, 1.18.2, 22w11a, 22w14a, 22w17a, 1.19 Pre-release 1 (includes snapshots)
Observed Behavior:
When multiple turtle eggs occupy the same block, breaking them one at a time by stepping on them does not produce a sculk vibration for each egg. The first eggs are removed by reducing the block’s `EGGS` property, but these removals do not activate a nearby sculk sensor. The sensor only detects the final egg being broken, when the turtle egg block is removed entirely.

As a result, a nearby sculk sensor receives one `BLOCK_DESTROY` vibration for the entire stack instead of detecting each individual turtle egg that is broken.
Expected Behavior: When turtle eggs occupying the same block are broken, each egg-breaking event should produce a detectable vibration, allowing a nearby sculk sensor to activate as the eggs are destroyed. The sensor should not detect only the final egg breaking; breaking any of the stacked eggs while stepping on them should trigger the expected sculk sensor response.
